title: Cough

rationale.RIPE therapy: Rifampin + INH + PZA + EMB x 2mo, then INH + RIF x 4mo. DOT.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with chronic cough >3 weeks, hemoptysis, night sweats, weight loss, fever, and fatigue. Risk factors: immigration from endemic area, HIV, homelessness, incarceration, healthcare exposure. TB is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis — acid-fast bacillus. CXR: apical infiltrates, cavitary lesions (reactivation TB), hilar lymphadenopathy, Ghon complex (primary). Diagnosis: sputum AFB smear (rapid, less sensitive), NAAT (PCR), mycobacterial culture (gold standard, results in weeks). IGRA (QuantiFERON) or PPD for latent TB screening — positive in active and latent. Airborne isolation (negative pressure room, N95). Treatment: RIPE therapy — Rifampin, Isoniazid, Pyrazinamide, Ethambutol for 2 months then INH + rifampin for 4 months. Directly observed therapy (DOT) preferred. Monitor LFTs (hepatotoxicity), vision (ethambutol → optic neuritis). Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) with INH to prevent neuropathy. Report to public health.
